content: Through pride we are ever deceiving ourselves. But deep down, below the surface of the average conscience, a still small voice says to us: something is out of tune.
author: Carl Jung
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

Carl Jung understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
